generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: THIS AI JUST CREATED VIRUSES NOT FOUND IN NATURE
Summary: Researchers have used AI to create new kinds of viruses for the first time. They taught AI to recognize patterns of DNA structure in nature and then use that data to write recipes for entirely new viruses. The researchers followed those recipes to create DNA molecules, which they inserted into bacteria. The viruses were able to infect other bacteria, demonstrating that they were viable.

Editorial idea:
AI can now move from recognizing biological patterns to producing viable biological agents, narrowing the distance between computation and real-world consequence.

Central subject:
AI-designed viruses demonstrated to infect bacteria

Visual relationship:
A sequence of abstract DNA instructions becomes a visibly viable biological form, showing the factual progression from machine-generated design to laboratory-tested infection.

Composition:
Use a grounded laboratory metaphor: a long strip of handwritten biological instructions passes through a precise pattern-reading process and emerges as several unfamiliar virus forms approaching a bacterial culture dish. Keep the transformation continuous rather than depicting a generic computer system.

Permitted literal elements:
DNA sequence patterns
newly designed virus forms
bacterial culture dish
laboratory testing context

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
artist imitation
rendered text
logos
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not imply the viruses infect humans or animals.
Do not depict a specific pathogen, outbreak, or weapon.
Do not suggest the AI independently performed the laboratory work.
Do not use generic futuristic computer imagery disconnected from the reported biological workflow.

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
